kept.q: A trader's wooden crate of mass 50 kg rests on a rough floor. If the coefficient of friction between the crate and the floor is 0.2, calculate the minimum horizontal force needed to just start the crate moving. (g = 10 m/s^2)
kept.explanation: The limiting friction force equals the coefficient of friction multiplied by the normal reaction (weight), which is 0.2 x 50 x 10 = 100 N. This is the minimum force to overcome friction and start motion.

kept.explanation: Taking the initial direction as positive, change in momentum = 0.2x(-10) - 0.2x(15) = -2 - 3 = -5 kg m/s. Force = change in momentum / time = 5/0.05 = 100 N, since the rebound reverses direction, the magnitudes of momentum change add up.

kept.q: A machine fires out small pellets of mass 0.01 kg each at a rate of 200 pellets per second, with each pellet leaving at a velocity of 50 m/s. Calculate the average force exerted on the machine due to the firing of the pellets.
kept.explanation: Force equals the rate of change of momentum, which is (mass per pellet x velocity x number fired per second) = 0.01 x 50 x 200 = 100 N. This treats the continuous stream of pellets as a steady momentum transfer per second.

q.q: Two spheres, P of mass 3 kg moving at 6 m/s and Q of mass 2 kg moving at 4 m/s in the same direction, collide and stick together. Calculate the common velocity of the combined spheres just after collision.
q.explanation: By conservation of momentum, (3x6 + 2x4) = (3+2)v, so 26 = 5v, giving v = 5.2 m/s. This is a perfectly inelastic collision where the bodies move together after impact.

q.q: A 2 kg block is placed on a smooth horizontal table and connected by a light inextensible string over a frictionless pulley to a 3 kg mass hanging freely. Calculate the acceleration of the system when released from rest. (g = 10 m/s^2)
q.explanation: The only driving force is the weight of the hanging mass, mg = 30 N, and the total mass being accelerated is 2+3 = 5 kg. Using a = F/total mass gives a = 30/5 = 6 m/s^2.

q.q: A body of mass 1500 g moves with a velocity of 8 m/s. Calculate the kinetic energy and the magnitude of linear momentum of the body respectively.
q.explanation: Mass is 1500 g = 1.5 kg. Kinetic energy = half x mass x velocity squared = 0.5 x 1.5 x 64 = 48 J, and momentum = mass x velocity = 1.5 x 8 = 12 kg m/s.
